title: Sprint 6d: the secrets file made once, and each repository's agent at one click

steps.say:
6d-1. What this walk needs, all on the laptop in your own account. Nothing is rented.

- keepassxc-cli: run from the checkout, the interface brings none of its own. Once, in a terminal of your own (it asks your sudo password): sudo apt install keepassxc-minimal
- Any project on this computer, for the secrets file (part 1).
- The test machine of this walk for the agents (part 2): frontend@192.168.122.174, Porelo 0.5.1~snapshot.344 or later, with the project f148walk: its repositories alpha (going by Alpha) and beta name the agent stub, gamma names none. Its key is ~/.claude/.ssh/claude_key; give ssh that key for the address with these lines in ~/.ssh/config:

Host 192.168.122.174
    IdentityFile ~/.claude/.ssh/claude_key
    IdentitiesOnly yes

Without them ssh offers other keys first, the machine refuses them, and after a few refusals it refuses this laptop for some minutes.

The walk itself starts from ~/git/porelo-frontend: mkdir -p ~/.porelo/walk && cp doc/walks/18-sprint-6d-the-secrets-file-and-the-agents.json ~/.porelo/walk/walk.json && PORELO_WALK=$HOME/.porelo/walk flutter run -d linux

This panel moves on by itself when it sees what a step waits for; where you are ahead of it, or a step is already done, click Next in this panel. Expected: the interface opens with this panel beside it. Once all of this is in place, click Next in this panel.

6d-2. Part 1, the secrets file. In the rail on the left click Projects, click your project, then the menu button beside its title (What … can be told to do) and Put this project on a server…. Expected: the wizard Put the project … on a server opens at step 1 of 7, Where it is rented.

6d-3. Fill steps 1 to 3 (Where it is rented, The project, Your ssh keys) as for a real setup and click Next after each; nothing is rented before the last step. Stop at step 4 of 7, Your secrets file: do not click Next there. Expected: its field shows ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx (your home's Porelo folder); with no file there yet it says setup makes it with a master password you choose, and the button says Make it now.

6d-4. Where keepassxc-cli is missing, the step says so above the button with an error mark and gives sudo apt install keepassxc-minimal in a box with a copy button; the button then says Make it now (try again), and each click looks again. With keepassxc-cli there, click Make it now (Open it now, where the file is there already). Expected: a terminal opens inside this program and asks a master password. Where the step says Ready: the file keeps the server's keys already, this was done before: click Next in this panel twice.

6d-5. In the terminal, type a new master password and press Enter, then the same again (for a file that is there: its master password once). Expected: nothing you type is shown, then The secrets file is ready. Click Done below the terminal.
6d-6. Expected on the step, below the button: Ready: the file keeps the server's keys. Click Leave at the bottom of the wizard and confirm: nothing is rented.

6d-7. In a terminal of your own (it asks your master password):

keepassxc ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx

Expected: the groups shared and hosts, and under hosts/<your project> the entries wireguard and vault-passphrase, each with a password set. Close KeePassXC, then click Next in this panel.

6d-8. Part 2, the agents: watch the test machine. In the rail click Machines, then Add a machine at the top of the page (the monitor with a plus at the top right opens the same).

1. What to call it: vm
2. Are you an administrator there? No: somebody else set Porelo up there for me
3. How to reach it: Raise the forward for me
4. Click Next.

Expected: the second page asks Where it is and Its socket, on that machine.

6d-9. Where it is: frontend@192.168.122.174
Its socket, on that machine: /run/user/1006/porelo/porelod.sock

This panel moves on once both are filled.
6d-10. Click Try the connection. Expected: it says Reached Porelo 0.5.1~snapshot.344 (or later).
6d-11. Click Watch it. Expected: the dialog closes and Machines lists vm as Connected. This panel moves on.

6d-12. In the rail click Projects, then click f148walk (on vm). The first time vm is shown, a pane What vm can run opens with the machine's first check; on the test machine it says three things are worth knowing about (no configuration key pinned, f148walk unverified, leftovers), which is as prepared: close it with the ✕ at its top right, beside Check again. Then click the menu button beside f148walk's title and Start an agent for each repository…. Expected: Which repositories, one row each: Agent Alpha starts as alpha in alpha and Agent beta starts as beta in beta, both checked; gamma names no agent, with nothing to check; a repository whose agent runs already says so.

6d-13. Uncheck Agent beta (it then says beta is left out), then click Next. Expected on Sign-ins: on the test machine, the first time, Nothing is stored for Stub Agent on this machine yet, with a button Sign in to Stub Agent; once signed in, The machine says every agent to start can start.

6d-14. Click Sign in to Stub Agent (where the step already says every agent can start, click Next in this panel). Expected: a window Log in with Stub Agent opens with a terminal running the sign-in on vm; the first time it says it is still working while f148walk's image is built, which takes some minutes. The stub needs nothing typed: it says stub: logged in, and the window says Signed in to Stub Agent: the credential is stored on vm. Click Done. The step has asked again by itself and says The machine says every agent to start can start. Click Next.

6d-15. Read the summary (Agent Alpha starts, beta is left out), then click Start them. Expected: the row says Agent Alpha is starting, then Agent Alpha started (or continues, for one brought back); a refused row says it was not started with the machine's words. The first start on a project never prepared waits for its image to be built, which takes some minutes.

6d-16. Click Leave at the bottom of the wizard, then open the menu beside f148walk's title and Start an agent for each repository… once more. Expected: Agent beta, left out, is offered with its box; Agent Alpha says Agent Alpha runs already, as alpha, with nothing to check. Click Leave without starting. Then tell me in this panel what differed; I stop the walk's tasks on vm afterwards.
